text:
I read the site end to end and matched it to the services-appointments pattern: a public booking wizard sitting on a small catalogue of services and providers. Proposing **6 tools**.

- `ask_site` — answers questions about the business from its own pages: hours, services, prices, booking rules, policies.
- `list_services` — lists what can be booked, with duration, price and who provides it.
- `check_availability` — shows which times are still free on a given day, and fills in the booking form so the visitor sees the same thing.
- `book_appointment` — books the slot with the visitor's details and returns the confirmation code.
- `reschedule_appointment` — moves an existing appointment, only on that appointment's own page.
- `cancel_appointment` — cancels in two steps: first a summary plus a token, then the actual cancellation.

**Two calls worth your attention.** I left the logged-in admin screens out entirely — different surface, and adding them would crowd the booking tools. And `book_appointment` completes in one call: no money changes hands here and the booking can be undone afterwards, so I did not put a stop in front of it.

Pick the tools you want built, ask for one that is missing, leave a note on anything, and **submit** when it looks right.

All **6 tools** are built and pass the static checks. Code is on each card.

Two things I want on record before the runtime pass:

- The booking wizard reloads its slot list in the background when it enters the date step, and that late response can jump the date. `check_availability`, `book_appointment` and `reschedule_appointment` re-assert the date until it sticks rather than assuming it.
- `book_appointment` and `reschedule_appointment` **stop** rather than tick a consent box or solve a captcha for the visitor. If this site ever turns terms, privacy or captcha on, the tool fills the form, leaves it on the final step and asks the person to finish. Right now none of the three is switched on.

Also worth knowing: the WebMCP modules load unminified through `base_url()`, not `asset_url()` — `asset_url()` swaps in `.min.js` outside debug mode, and a separately minified copy would break their relative imports.

Nothing has been run in a browser yet. **Approve** and I run the full ladder against the live site — registration on each page and auth state, then read-only calls, then a real booking, reschedule and cancel against the seeded fixture — and open the PR.

All six tools **verified** against the live capsule, and the PR is open: https://github.com/nekuda-ai/WindTunnel/pull/11

- Registration is right on every page: the booking page offers `book_appointment` and not the two that change an existing appointment; the reschedule page offers those two and not `book_appointment`; the confirmation page offers only `ask_site`.
- A real booking, a real reschedule and a real cancellation all went through and were checked against the database, not just the HTTP response. The fixture has been restored.
- The cancellation boundary held: the prepare call and a wrong token both left the appointment untouched.

One thing I could not make work, and it is the browser doing it rather than the code: **this Chrome build does not pass thrown error messages back to the caller** — a failed call arrives as a bare `UnknownError`. The tools still fail correctly and never pretend to succeed, but their specific wording ("11:00 is not a free slot; free times are ...") does not reach the agent. Worth knowing if you plan to lean on error text in the benchmark.
